info.title: Trovy API
info.description:
The Trovy loyalty engine, for a partner's own backend: instant rewards and gift cards behind your own checkout. Trovy handles no payments.

## Authentication

Every request carries a secret key: `Authorization: Bearer trv_live_…` against production, `Authorization: Bearer trv_test_…` against the sandbox. Keys belong on your server only — never in a mobile app or a web page. Your team creates, rotates and revokes them in the Trovy dashboard.

## Sandbox

Your team makes its own sandbox in the Trovy dashboard (Integrations → Developer API → Create sandbox): a test copy of your business, with its own test keys. `https://api.sandbox.trovy.ca` runs the same API against it. Test keys only work there, and live keys only against production. No text message ever leaves a sandbox: every response that would have sent one carries the rendered message in `sms.preview`. Its sign-up form accepts only fictional phone numbers (a US or Canadian area code, or 721, then 555-0100 to 555-0199), so a sandbox can never reach a real person.

## Idempotency

Every request that changes something takes an `Idempotency-Key` header. Retrying with the same key returns the original result, so a timed-out call can never earn twice or charge a gift card twice. Reusing a key with a different body is refused.

## Errors

Errors are `{ "error": "…", "code": "…", "requestId": "…" }`. `code` is stable and documented on each operation; quote `requestId` when you email hello@trovy.ca. A 401 means fix your credentials (rotate the key); a 403 means the key is recognised and something else forbids the call.

## Rate limits

Limits are per key. Every response carries `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset`; a 429 adds `Retry-After`.

## Versioning

The version is in the path. Changes within `/v1` are additive: new endpoints, new optional fields, new error codes. Anything that would break a working integration ships as `/v2`.

bearerAuth.description: A secret key: trv_live_… against production, trv_test_… against the sandbox.

environment.description: Which deployment answered. Test keys only ever see `sandbox`.

timezone.description: IANA zone the business reports in.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code every `...Cents` field in this API is counted in. One business has one currency and it never changes once it has transacted, so read it once at setup rather than per call.

rewardRateBps.description: Reward rate in basis points: 500 = 5% of the order.

capCents.description: Most a customer's waiting reward can grow to, in cents. `null` means uncapped.

minRedemptionPurchaseCents.description: An order must reach this, in cents, before a reward can be applied to it.

rewardValidityDays.description: Days a reward stays redeemable once it becomes usable.

redemptionDelayDays.description: Whole days, in your business's timezone, before a newly earned reward can be applied: 0 = right away, 1 = from the next day.

recurring.description: When true, an order that redeems a reward earns again on the remainder.

Program.description: The active rewards program, or `null` when none is linked to the Developer API yet.

x-enumDescriptions.API_KEY_INVALID: The key is malformed, unknown, or minted for the other environment.
x-enumDescriptions.API_KEY_REVOKED: The key was revoked. Create a new one in the dashboard.
x-enumDescriptions.API_KEY_DISABLED: Trovy disabled this key. Contact hello@trovy.ca — rotating will not help.
x-enumDescriptions.API_KEY_WRONG_TYPE: A Shopify or publishable key was sent where a secret key is required.
x-enumDescriptions.API_NOT_ENABLED: The Developer API is not enabled for this business.
x-enumDescriptions.VALIDATION_ERROR: The request failed validation; `details` lists the issues.
x-enumDescriptions.NOT_FOUND: No such route, or no such resource for this business.
x-enumDescriptions.LINK_TOKEN_INVALID: The link token is unknown, expired, already used, or was issued for another business. The customer verifies again in the widget.
x-enumDescriptions.CUSTOMER_NOT_FOUND: No member of your business matches — the phone number is not a member's, or the customer id is not one of yours.
x-enumDescriptions.IDEMPOTENCY_MISMATCH: This `Idempotency-Key` was already used for a request with a different body. Use a new key for a new order event.
x-enumDescriptions.DUPLICATE_ORDER: An order with this `orderId` is already recorded for your business. Order ids are unique per business.
x-enumDescriptions.ACTIVE_REWARD_EXISTS: The customer has a usable reward waiting (`details.reward`). An order applies it with `POST /v1/redeem` or records nothing; it cannot earn on top. A reward that is not usable yet never blocks an earn: the order adds to it.
x-enumDescriptions.NO_ACTIVE_PROGRAM: Your business has no active rewards program linked to the Developer API.
x-enumDescriptions.FIRST_ORDER_ONLY: The program rewards a customer's first order only, and this customer has already earned.
x-enumDescriptions.STORE_NOT_FOUND: `storeId` is not one of your active locations (`GET /v1/stores`).
x-enumDescriptions.REWARD_NOT_FOUND: No such reward for this customer at your business.
x-enumDescriptions.REWARD_NOT_YET_USABLE: The program holds a newly earned reward back until `details.usableFrom` (a local midnight at your business), so it can't be applied to the order that earned it or to another order that day.
x-enumDescriptions.REWARD_VOIDED: The reward was cancelled by refunds of the orders that earned it.
x-enumDescriptions.REWARD_CHANGED: The reward changed between your read and this call (a refund landed). Read it again.
x-enumDescriptions.NOT_OLDEST_REWARD: Rewards are redeemed oldest first; `details.oldestRewardId` is the one to apply.
x-enumDescriptions.MINIMUM_ORDER_NOT_MET: The order does not reach the reward's minimum; `details.minimumOrderCents`.
x-enumDescriptions.ORDER_NOT_FOUND: No order with this `orderId` was recorded through the API for your business.
x-enumDescriptions.ORDER_AMBIGUOUS: More than one purchase is recorded under this `orderId`. Email hello@trovy.ca.
x-enumDescriptions.REFUND_EXCEEDS_REMAINING: `amountCents` is more than what is left to refund; `details.remainingRefundableCents`.
x-enumDescriptions.ALREADY_FULLY_REFUNDED: The order has already been fully refunded.
x-enumDescriptions.GIFT_CARDS_NOT_ENABLED: Gift-card issuance is not enabled for your business. Contact Trovy to enable it.
x-enumDescriptions.AMOUNT_OUT_OF_RANGE: The amount is outside your business's gift-card limits; `details` carries them.
x-enumDescriptions.DAILY_CAP_REACHED: Issuing this card would pass your daily gift-card limit; `details` carries the cap and what is left. It resets at 00:00 UTC.
x-enumDescriptions.GIFT_CARD_NOT_FOUND: No gift card with this code or id belongs to your business.
x-enumDescriptions.GIFT_CARD_NOT_REDEEMABLE: The card is spent out, voided, or not yet active; `details.balanceCents` is what is left.
x-enumDescriptions.INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE: The card does not hold this much; `details.balanceCents` is what is left.
x-enumDescriptions.NOT_YOUR_GIFT_CARD: This card was sold by Trovy, not by you, so only Trovy can cancel it.
x-enumDescriptions.REDEMPTION_NOT_FOUND: No gift-card redemption with this id belongs to your business.
x-enumDescriptions.NOT_REVERSIBLE: This debit cannot be put back: the card is voided, or the row is itself a reversal.
x-enumDescriptions.EXCEEDS_REVERSIBLE: More than this debit can still put back; `details.reversibleCents` is the remainder.
x-enumDescriptions.INTERNAL_ERROR: Something failed on our side. Quote `requestId` when you email hello@trovy.ca.

requestId.description: Identifies this request in Trovy's logs. Quote it when you email hello@trovy.ca.

details.description: The failing fields on a 400; on several 409s the value to act on (see each code).

isDefault.description: The location orders are attributed to when none is given.

id.description: Your customer id for this member — see `Customer`.

isNew.description: True when this verification created the trovy account; false when an existing member linked to you.

linkToken.description: The one-time token the sign-up widget handed your page (`onSuccess`, or your link route). Valid for five minutes, exchangeable once.

linked.description: Whether this member has linked to your business through the sign-up widget. Only a linked member has an id you can act on; for anyone else, show the widget.

id.description: Your customer id for this member. Store it against your own account record; every rewards and gift-card call takes it. It means nothing at any other business.

name.description: First name, as the member gave it.

phone.description: A North American number. Formatting is ignored: `+14165550100`, `14165550100` and `(416) 555-0100` are the same number.

rewards.description: Usable rewards first, then soonest-expiring. Normally zero or one: a customer redeems a usable reward before they earn again.

valueCents.description: What the reward is worth, in cents. It grows as the customer earns again before redeeming.

minimumOrderCents.description: An order must reach this, in cents, to have the reward applied.

expiresAt.description: ISO 8601. `null` means it does not expire.

usableFrom.description: ISO 8601. The first moment the reward can be applied. A program with a redemption delay holds a new reward back until a local midnight at your business, so it can't be spent on the order that earned it.

usable.description: Whether `usableFrom` has passed. Decide at checkout from this flag, not from the list being non-empty: a customer whose only reward is not usable yet earns (`earnReward`), and the order adds to that reward.

replayed.description: True when this is the stored result of an earlier call with the same `Idempotency-Key`; nothing was recorded twice.

earnedCents.description: What this order added to the customer's reward, in cents. 0 when the order was too small to earn — rewards round to whole dollars.

allOf.description: The customer's reward after this order — its full value, not just this order's share. `null` when nothing was earned.

transactionId.description: Trovy's id for this order. Quote it when you email hello@trovy.ca.

id.description: Your order id, as you sent it.

status.description: `sent`: the customer was texted. `preview`: sandbox — nothing was sent and `preview` holds the text. `failed`: the text could not be sent; the order and reward still stand. `not_sent`: nothing to say (no reward, or a replay).

preview.description: Sandbox only: the full text the customer would have received.

orderId.description: Your own order id. Unique per business — recording a second order under the same id is refused with `DUPLICATE_ORDER` — and what a refund names later.

amountCents.description: The order total in cents, before any reward is taken off.

storeId.description: Which of your locations fulfilled the order (`listStores`). Defaults to your default location. Reporting only — a reward earned at one location is redeemable at any.

replayed.description: True when this is the stored result of an earlier call with the same `Idempotency-Key`; nothing was recorded twice.

redeemedCents.description: What came off the order: the reward's full value, in cents.

allOf.description: On a recurring program, the reward this order earned on what the customer actually paid. Otherwise `null`.

transactionId.description: Trovy's id for this order. Quote it when you email hello@trovy.ca.

orderId.description: Your own order id. Unique per business — recording a second order under the same id is refused with `DUPLICATE_ORDER` — and what a refund names later.

amountCents.description: The order total in cents, before any reward is taken off.

storeId.description: Which of your locations fulfilled the order (`listStores`). Defaults to your default location. Reporting only — a reward earned at one location is redeemable at any.

replayed.description: True when this is the stored result of an earlier call with the same `Idempotency-Key`; nothing was recorded twice.

rewardReversedCents.description: Reward value taken back from the customer, in cents, in proportion to the refund. 0 when there was nothing live to take back — see `rewardAdjustment`.

paidCents.description: What the customer actually paid: the total less any reward applied.

refundedCents.description: Refunded so far, this call included.

reward.description: The reward the order earned, after this refund. `null` when the order earned none.

rewardAdjustment.description: `applied`: the live reward was reduced by `rewardReversedCents`. `nothing_earned`: the order earned no reward. `already_reversed`: earlier refunds already took back all it earned. `reward_redeemed` / `reward_expired` / `reward_voided` / `reward_missing`: the reward is no longer live, so nothing was taken back.

orderId.description: The order you refunded, as you recorded it with `earnReward` or `redeemReward`.

amountCents.description: What you refunded the customer, in cents. Partial refunds are fine; across calls the total can never exceed what they paid.

replayed.description: True when this is the stored result of an earlier call with the same `Idempotency-Key`; nothing was recorded twice.

id.description: Trovy's id for the card. A void names it.

faceValueCents.description: What the card was sold for.

status.description: `active`: spendable. `depleted`: spent out, and it can come back to `active` if a redemption is reversed. `voided`: cancelled, never spendable again.

externalRef.description: Your own reference, as you sent it.

customerId.description: The buyer — a member of your business, from `linkCustomer`. A card always has a buyer on record.

amountCents.description: What the buyer paid you, in cents. Your business's limits apply.

externalRef.description: Your own reference for the sale, carried on the card.

message.description: A note from the buyer to the recipient.

issuedByYou.description: True when you sold this card. A card Trovy sold is still redeemable at your checkout; only you can void your own.

code.description: The code on the card. Case is ignored.

replayed.description: True when this is the stored result of an earlier call with the same `Idempotency-Key`; nothing was recorded twice.

redemptionId.description: The debit. `reverseGiftCardRedemption` names this id — a code never identifies a debit.

balanceCents.description: What is left after this debit.

depleted.description: True when the card is now spent out.

code.description: The code on the card. Case is ignored.

amountCents.description: What to take off the card, in cents. Partial is fine.

externalRef.description: The order you are settling, carried on the ledger row.

replayed.description: True when this is the stored result of an earlier call with the same `Idempotency-Key`; nothing was recorded twice.

reversalId.description: The reversal row. It cannot itself be reversed.

reversedCents.description: What went back onto the card.

balanceCents.description: The card's balance after the reversal.

amountCents.description: How much to put back. Defaults to everything this debit can still restore.

externalRef.description: Your refund's reference, carried on the reversal row.

alreadyVoided.description: True when the card was already void; nothing changed.

get.summary: Your business and its active rewards program
get.description: Use it to confirm a key is wired to the business you expect, and to read the program terms your checkout applies: the rate, the cap, and the minimum order a reward can be applied to.
Active locations, for attributing an order to the one that fulfilled it. Attribution is reporting only — a reward can be earned at one location and redeemed at another.

post.summary: Exchange a sign-up widget token for a customer id
post.description: When the sign-up form hands your page a `linkToken` (`onSuccess`, or your link route), post it here from your server. The answer is the customer id you store against your own account record and pass to every rewards and gift-card call. A token is valid for five minutes and can be exchanged once; if your exchange fails or times out, have the customer verify again — their membership already exists, so it takes seconds.
post.x-trovy-idempotency-exempt: A link token is single-use by itself: a retry answers 404 and the member verifies again.

200.description: The member behind the token, as your business knows them.

post.summary: Find a member of your business by phone number
post.description: Tells you whether a phone number belongs to a member of your business, and whether that member has linked to you through the sign-up widget. Only a linked member has an id you can act on; for anyone else, show the widget. Non-members are a 404, so this is also how you decide whether to say "welcome back". Limited to 120 calls a minute per key.
post.x-trovy-idempotency-exempt: A read. It takes a POST only so the phone number travels in the body, never in a URL.

get.summary: A customer's rewards waiting to be redeemed
get.description: The customer's rewards at your business: usable ones first, then soonest-expiring. Normally zero or one: a customer redeems a usable reward before they earn again, and a new qualifying order grows the reward they already have. Call it when the customer reaches checkout: apply a reward with `POST /v1/redeem` when it is `usable` and the order reaches its minimum; otherwise record the order with `POST /v1/earn`, or nothing while a usable reward is waiting.

post.summary: Record an order and earn the customer a reward
post.description: Call it once the order is paid. The reward is the program's rate of the order total, rounded to whole dollars, so small orders can earn nothing (`earnedCents: 0`) — that is still a recorded order, not an error. A customer with a usable reward waiting cannot earn again until it is redeemed: the answer is 409 `ACTIVE_REWARD_EXISTS` with the reward in `details`, and your checkout should offer to apply it (`POST /v1/redeem`) instead. A reward the program is still holding back (`usable: false`) doesn't block: the order adds to it. Retrying with the same `Idempotency-Key` returns the original result with `replayed: true`.

schema.description: Sent as `Idempotency-Key` (header names are case-insensitive). The id your system already has for this event: your order id for an earn or redeem, your refund's own id for a refund. Retrying with the same key returns the original result (`replayed: true`); reusing it with a different body is refused with `IDEMPOTENCY_MISMATCH`. Letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, up to 128 characters.

200.description: The stored result of an earlier call with this Idempotency-Key.

post.summary: Apply a customer's reward to an order
post.description: Take the reward's `valueCents` off the order yourself, capture the rest, then call this once the order is paid. The order must reach the reward's `minimumOrderCents`. On a recurring program the order also earns a new reward on what the customer actually paid (`newReward`). Rewards are redeemed oldest first. A reward the program is still holding back (`usable: false`) is refused with `REWARD_NOT_YET_USABLE`. Retrying with the same `Idempotency-Key` returns the original result with `replayed: true`.

post.summary: Record a refund and adjust the reward it earned
post.description: Call it after you refund the customer, in full or in part; the total across calls can never exceed what they paid. The reward the order earned shrinks in proportion while it is still live — a reward already redeemed, expired or cancelled is left alone, and `rewardAdjustment` says which. Refunding an order that redeemed a reward never reinstates that reward; only the new reward the order earned is reduced. Retrying with the same `Idempotency-Key` returns the original result.

post.summary: Issue a gift card you have been paid for
post.description: Call it once the buyer has paid you. The card comes back active and spendable immediately — you hold the money, so there is nothing for Trovy to wait for. The buyer must be a member of your business, so the card has an owner on record. Your business has a daily issuance limit; going past it answers 409 `DAILY_CAP_REACHED` with what is left. Two issuances at your business at the same instant do not queue: one may answer 429 `RATE_LIMITED` with `Retry-After`, having issued nothing — send it again with the same `Idempotency-Key`. Retrying with the same `Idempotency-Key` returns the same card.

post.description: What the customer can still spend, before you take anything off. A card of another business is simply not found. `issuedByYou` is false for a card Trovy's own storefront sold: it spends at your checkout exactly the same, but only the seller can cancel it.

post.summary: Take an amount off a gift card
post.description: Call it **before** you capture payment for the order: the card is the customer's money, and a debit you cannot collect against is worse than a declined order. Partial amounts are fine. Keep the `redemptionId` — a refund later puts the money back by naming it. Retrying with the same `Idempotency-Key` returns the original debit without taking anything more.

post.description: When you refund an order you settled against a card, or the order failed after you debited it, this returns the money to the card. Partial and repeatable up to what the debit took; asking for more answers 409 `EXCEEDS_REVERSIBLE` with what is left. A card that was spent out comes back to `active`. A voided card is never restored, and a reversal cannot itself be reversed. Only a debit you made through the API can be put back; any other redemption id answers 404 `REDEMPTION_NOT_FOUND`.

post.summary: Cancel a gift card you issued
post.description: Stops the card being spent — for a sale you cancelled, or a card issued in error. The balance is left on the record, because you hold the buyer's money and refunding them is yours to do; Trovy only stops the card. You can only void a card you issued. Voiding twice is safe and changes nothing.
post.x-trovy-idempotency-exempt: Voiding is idempotent by nature: the card is either void or it now is.

schema.description: The card's `id`. Not its code — a code is a secret and never goes in a URL.
